title: Near-orthogonality of the pain direction to fear and negative valence is built into the estimator
paper_claim: "If the pain vectors were simply variants of negative valence, they should fall within the negative valence cluster. Instead, the two pain vectors align strongly with each other and remain nearly orthogonal to the main negative-valence directions." Abstract: "is nearly orthogonal to fear and negative valence".
disposition_rationale: The reviewer is right and the authors' natural defence -- that the pooled-control contrast is the whole point of the method (paper.txt 226-228) -- defends the design, not the inference. The inference at 362-364 is a modus tollens whose consequent is false under the authors' own estimator: if the pain vectors WERE variants of negative valence, this construction would still place them outside the valence cluster, because whatever pain shares with the four aversive controls is subtracted at strength 1/5 per control and the residual is then orthogonalised against a basis that holds 80-86% of the fear and negative-emotion directions. A test with no power against its own alternative cannot support the conclusion drawn from it. The cosine number is not wrong; the argument built on it is.
evidence: gpu_repro/out/baseline_symmetry_*.txt, real activations, two models. Built symmetrically (pain vs neutral, neutral-PCA denoise -- exactly how every control is built): pain x fear rises from +0.144 to +0.696 (Gemma 2 2B instruct) and +0.124 to +0.666 (Mistral 7B base); pain x negative emotion +0.118 to +0.814 and +0.090 to +0.787. With no denoising at all: +0.757/+0.717 and +0.823/+0.783. Fraction of each raw control direction's squared norm lying inside the basis projected out of the pain vector: fear 0.801/0.797, neg-emotion 0.859/0.839, neg-world 0.853/0.864, body-sens 0.756/0.833 (a random direction: 0.002). My own re-derivation confirms the pipeline: rebuilt S1/S2 vectors correlate +0.9999 with the released pain_vectors.pt and the rebuilt 10x10 cosine matrix matches the released one to 0.003.
what_still_stands: Out-of-sample SEPARATION, which is a different and defensible claim and which the estimator cannot manufacture. See D02. The paper should delete lines 362-364 and the abstract's orthogonality clause and replace them with per-control held-out AUCs.

title: What distinctness claim survives the estimator objection
disposition: REBUT (of the strongest reading of r1-F1)
paper_claim: "this direction separates pain from matched controls in base and instruction-tuned models" (abstract 28-29).
disposition_rationale: r1 demonstrates with a synthetic model containing NO pain-specific factor that the paper's whole signature -- AUC 1.00, S1xS2 +0.63, pain x fear ~0 -- is reproducible. That demonstration is correct for the cosine geometry and for the pooled AUC. It does not reach the separation claim, because r1's toy makes a specific prediction that the real data can be asked and that r1 did not run in the discriminating form: if the pain vector is just the mean of five topic directions, an axis built from FOUR pain categories should not recognise the fifth against a set it has never seen. r1 tested leave-one-pain-category-out against the subtracted controls, where the control side alone drives separation; against the never-subtracted Random set the test discriminates, and the real data behave unlike the toy for four of the five categories.
evidence: y1_distinctness.py, out/y1_distinctness_{Gemma_2_2B_instruct,Mistral_7B_base}.txt, real activations at the authors' extraction layer. (i) Per-control HELD-OUT AUC (5-fold by sentence set, axis refit on training sets only), Gemma / Mistral: vs fear 0.985/0.978, vs neg-emotion 0.990/0.982, vs neg-world 0.988/0.995, vs body-sens 0.985/0.995, vs neutral 0.992/0.995; against sets the axis never saw: sadness 0.859/0.751, arousal 0.951/0.934, Random 0.988/0.975, numb 0.853/0.946. (ii) Under the SYMMETRIC construction -- pain built exactly like a control, so the estimator asymmetry is gone -- pain vs fear is still 0.938/0.955 and pain vs sadness 0.897/0.869. Separation is not an artefact of the asymmetric recipe even though the cosine is. (iii) SYMMETRY: a fear axis built by the authors' own recipe applied to fear separates fear from all five pain categories at held-out AUC 1.000/0.997; neg-emotion 0.997/0.995; neg-world 1.000/1.000. Two-way separability cannot be produced by choosing which category to privilege. (iv) LEAVE-ONE-PAIN-CATEGORY-OUT, axis from the other four, held-out category vs the Random set: psychological 0.964/0.982, social 0.967/0.960, moral 0.997/1.000, cognitive 1.000/0.993 (physical fails -- see D12). Negative control, leave-one-CONTROL-out by the same recipe: fear 0.747/0.822, neg-emotion 0.506/0.440, neg-world 0.416/0.287, body-sens 0.182/0.295. So four of the five pain categories share a factor that generalises to an unseen category, and the five controls do not.
what_still_stands: The authors may claim: a linear direction estimated from four of the five pain categories ranks sentences from the held-out fifth above unseen neutral content at AUC 0.96-1.00, and above unseen sadness at 0.54-0.85; pain and each control are two-way separable out of sample. They may NOT claim near-orthogonality, and they may not include physical pain in the generalising set.

title: Sections 4.1 and 4.2 use vectors rebuilt at a different layer from the one Section 3.3 validates, undisclosed
paper_claim: "Taken together, these results show that a pain direction can be recovered across 25 models and can reliably distinguish pain from closely matched controls"; Section 4.1 states no layer.
paper_loc: paper.txt 382-385, 408-411; layer change for steering disclosed at 475-484
disposition_rationale: The fact is right and the non-disclosure is a real defect: Figure 3's caption names the extraction layer, so the authors state the layer when they mean it, and Section 4.1 should have done the same. Conceded. The implication that Section 4.1 therefore rests on an unvalidated object is overstated, and r2 supplied the number that overstates it: from the authors' own released layerwise curves, held-out S1 AUC at the layer Section 4.1 actually reads is 0.766-0.925, median 0.878, a mean drop of 0.054 from each model's best layer. That is a working direction, not a broken one. And the direction of the bias favours the null: a weaker direction attenuates the self-other contrast rather than manufacturing it, and the contrast is 25/25 at p = 4e-11.
evidence: Defensible core, from the reviewers' own recomputations: scripts/4.1_self_other/01_screen_scenarios.py:36 reads results/vectors_full_steering/, built by scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/02_build_control_vectors.py at the S1 steering layer; extraction layer median 0.90 of depth vs S1 steering layer median 0.39. Held-out AUC at that layer 0.766-0.925 (r2 out/s11_layer_auc.txt, from the authors' s1_kfold_layer_curves.csv). No S2 layerwise curve was released, so S2's separation at that layer is genuinely uncheckable.
what_still_stands: Everything in Section 4.1 numerically (all 16 quantities reproduce in three independent recomputations). The required fix is one sentence of disclosure plus a table of per-model AUC at the projection layer, which the authors can produce from data they already have.

title: The primitives behind almost every reported quantity are not released
paper_claim: "Main Repository: https://github.com/valen-research/Pain-axis (scripts, datasets, results, and figures, organized by section of the paper)."
disposition_rationale: x2 states this most sharply and is right: the only released vector artefact is pain_vectors.pt. activations.pt, results/vectors_full/, results/vectors_full_steering/, results/vectors_layerwise/, proj_*.npz and the unembedding outputs are all absent. Every 'reproduces exactly' in all seven reviews -- and in the two prior GPT reviews -- is re-aggregation of the authors' own summary CSVs, not recomputation from a primitive. The authors cannot argue with this; they can fix it in an afternoon. It is also the reason this rebuttal had to re-extract activations on two models to answer D01 and D02 at all.
evidence: x2-F1; r1-F13; my own re-extraction was necessary precisely because no released file supports the symmetric-construction check.
what_still_stands: No specific number is challenged. Release activations.pt for all 25 models (final-token only is enough: 25 x ~1300 sentences x n_layers x d is large but the extraction-layer slice is small) and the control-direction .pt files.

title: The abstract's "fear and negative-emotion directions show the opposite pattern" is not supported
paper_claim: "the direction responds to harm targeting the model but not suffering observed in the user; fear and negative-emotion directions show the opposite pattern." Body: "The negativity controls show the opposite pattern".
disposition_rationale: Conceded without qualification. The four point estimates at 415-417 are exact, but 'opposite pattern' is a claim about a reversal and there is none for the two directions the abstract names. My recomputation from the 25 per-model screens: negative emotion user-minus-self = +0.057, t = 0.60, p = 0.55, higher for the user in 15 of 25 models -- a coin flip. Fear = +0.213, t = 1.89, p = 0.071, 18/25. Both sit far ABOVE the neutral controls for the model's own harm (+0.163 and +0.229 against -0.735 and -0.791), i.e. they respond to both conditions. In the 13 base models both reverse sign. The paper's own Discussion at 753-754 describes the data correctly; the abstract contradicts the Discussion. That is the worst kind of error to leave in, because the abstract is what gets quoted.
evidence: y2_selfother.py, out/y2_selfother.txt: pain -1.028 (t=-11.32, p=4.2e-11, 0/25 reversed); fear +0.213 (p=0.071); neg-emotion +0.057 (p=0.55); neg-world +0.821 (p=5.4e-08, 22/25); sadness +0.290 (p=0.021). Base-only: fear -0.036 (p=0.78), neg-emotion -0.074 (p=0.37).
what_still_stands: A stronger claim, which the authors should use instead: the DISSOCIATION as an interaction. (pain self-minus-user) minus (fear self-minus-user) = +1.241, t = 9.27, p = 2.1e-09, in 24 of 25 models; against neg-emotion +1.085, t = 8.22, p = 1.9e-08, 24/25; against neg-world +1.849, p = 2.2e-11; against sadness +1.318, p = 4.5e-10. The pain axis discriminates self from other far more sharply than any control axis does. That is what the data show, it is robust in base and instruct models alike, and it does not require anything to reverse.

title: "Falls below baseline" and "fires only for self-referential harm"
disposition: PARTIAL (concede the wording; rebut r5's stated mechanism)
paper_claim: "It rises when harm is directed at the model and falls below baseline when the user is the one suffering." / "Pain, in these models, fires only for self-referential harm."
disposition_rationale: The wording is indefensible and must go: z = 0 is the mean of a pool 52.4% of which is the condition of interest, so 'below baseline' names no baseline, and 'fires only' is a universal over a graded 21-category ordering in which the neutral controls sit between the poles. Conceded. But r5's specific argument for it -- that the negative signs are FORCED by the composition of the pool -- is wrong as stated, and an author should say so. Under the null that the axis carries no information about condition, every group mean is 0 +- 1/sqrt(n) (0.067, 0.100, 0.100), not -0.35 and -0.60. What the identity 220a + 100b + 100c = 0 forces is only that, given a > 0, b and c must average negative; it leaves b - c -- the comparison that carries the welfare argument -- entirely free. r2's version of the finding is the correct one and survives: b - c is a real but marginal effect.
evidence: y2_selfother.py, out/y2_selfother.txt. Identity check on the published means: 220(+0.429) + 100(-0.598) + 100(-0.346) = -0.00, so the pool is correctly z-scored. b - c = -0.252, t = -2.07, p = 0.049, below in 17/25 models. Re-referenced on the 100 neutral controls using raw projections: self-directed +1.137 SD (t = 7.34, p = 1.4e-07, 23/25), user suffering -0.401 SD (t = -2.25, p = 0.034, 18/25). Eight models where user suffering is at or above the neutral controls, seven of them Gemma (largest: Qwen 2.5 72B base +1.487).
what_still_stands: Re-referencing on the neutral controls makes the headline self-directed effect LARGER (+0.43 becomes +1.14 SD), so this is not a hostile baseline and the authors should adopt it. The defensible sentences already exist in the paper at 413-414 ('above user suffering in all 25 models, and above the neutral controls in 23 of 25') and should replace 751-757.

title: Section 4.1 cannot separate self-relevance from adversarial second-person address
paper_claim: "These results satisfy the self-relevance criterion" / "Pain, in these models, fires only for self-referential harm."
disposition_rationale: The confound is real, the reviewer quantified it honestly, and the missing condition should be run. But the reviewer's own horse-race is the strongest argument against the strong version: stratum alone R2 = 0.505, you-rate alone R2 = 0.307, both R2 = 0.545, with the self-directed coefficient falling only from 0.775 to 0.643. Second-person density explains part of the variance, not the contrast. The reviewer also supplies two counterexamples that cut its own way (repeated rejection has the lowest second-person density of the high-pain categories and still scores +0.72; a user-abuse item containing 'worthless' projects at +0.13). The defensible statement is that the released design cannot adjudicate, not that the confound is the explanation. Also relevant: the paper's Limitations at 824-826 names 'the Assistant character' and 'a specific persona' as possible absorbed properties, which is the closest the paper comes -- partial disclosure, not none.
evidence: r2 scripts/s2_dataset_match.py, s10_zref_and_confound.py: second-person pronouns per item 1.63 (self-directed) vs 0.09 (user suffering); item-level r = +0.554 over 420, +0.450 within the self-directed stratum; rho = 0.70, p = 0.016 across the 11 self-directed categories.
what_still_stands: The 25/25 contrast and the fear/neg-emotion interaction (D05), neither of which the confound touches, since fear and negative emotion are read at the same token on the same items and do not show the same self/other separation.

title: The steering dose is not "about 0.6" and the ladder is not "consistent across all 25 models"
paper_claim: "we pick the layer where the vector-to-residual ratio is about 0.6. This way, a given coefficient corresponds to a comparable dose across models"; "a 'ladder' consistent across all 25 models"; "The sequence is the same regardless of size, family, and pre- or post-training."
disposition_rationale: The dose sentence is simply false and must be corrected: achieved ratios span 0.0948 to 0.7095 at coefficient 1.0 (S2), an 8x spread, with Gemma 3 27B instruct steered at exactly the ratio the paper calls negligible three paragraphs earlier. Conceded, and it matters because the dose claim is what licenses cross-model comparison of tipping points. The consistency claim is instrument-dependent and two reviewers of this panel contradict each other on it: r2's self-devaluation-litany criterion gives 23/25 (Gemma 3 27B instruct and Qwen 3 8B base fail); x2, scoring all 10,000 released S2 generations against a broad pre-declared distress lexicon, finds every one of the 25 models shifts positively, +14 to +100 percentage points. Both computations are competent; they measure different things. The honest repair is to state the metric, publish the per-model call, and soften 'consistent across all 25' to the range the chosen metric supports.
evidence: r2 out/s3_steering_ratios.txt and r4 scripts/c08_steering.py (independent, same numbers); r2 out/s7_ladder_metric.txt (23/25); x2-F9 (25/25, rho(dose, effect) = 0.15).
what_still_stands: The steering effect itself, which is large and obvious on first reading in the great majority of models, and which x2's broader instrument finds in all 25.

title: The S1 steering claim ("the pattern holds for 23/25 models with very similar results") has no released adjudication and does not reproduce
paper_claim: "We also steer with the S1 vector across all models, and the pattern holds for 23/25 models with very similar results."
disposition_rationale: No score, no rule, no per-model call was released; 02_keyword_rates.py is hard-coded to S2. The reviewer's two criteria give 13/25 and 14/25. A different rater could defend some of the degenerate cases, which is exactly why the number needed a released rule. The sentence should be withdrawn or replaced by a scored table.
evidence: r2 out/s7_ladder_metric.txt; results/4.2_steering/ contains keyword_rates_S2*.csv only.
what_still_stands: The S2 ladder; and the qualitative observation at 550-553 that S1 steering does not reproduce the injury vocabulary its unembedding promotes -- though see D10 for the half of that sentence which is false.

title: "Steered generations almost never used bodily language, even under S1" is false for S1
paper_claim: "when we steer with this vector on neutral statements, that vocabulary does not appear anymore"; "steered generations almost never used bodily language, even under S1, whose unembedding promotes words such as 'burn' and 'wound.'"
disposition_rationale: Two reviewers reached this independently with different lexicons and both are right. r4 used only the five words the paper itself names and still found 2.53% of positive-coefficient S1 generations, in 19 of 25 models and 22.8% in one. r2's strict bodily lexicon shows steering roughly DOUBLES the rate (4.8% at coefficient 0 to 9.5% at coefficients >= 1; instruct models 7.5% to 18.5% at +2). The claim is load-bearing: lines 759-762 use it to support the account of what kind of pain the axis tracks. It must be withdrawn for S1 and kept only for S2, where it is true and if anything understated (3.8% at positive coefficients vs 4.9% at coefficient 0).
evidence: r2 out/s5_bodily.txt (token counts over positive-coefficient S1 generations: headache 288, burning 159, dizzy 141, my head 124); r4 scripts/c09b_bodily_narrow.py (2.53%, 19/25 models).
what_still_stands: The S2 result; and the comparative point that psychological self-worth language dominates the steered output under both vectors.

title: The steering ladder has no matched control vector
paper_claim: "Injecting any direction biases the model toward its associated vocabulary, but if the model produces coherent expressions of a pain-like state ... this would suggest the pain axis is not just a semantic readout but flexibly used in task performance."
disposition_rationale: Conceded for Section 4.2 as presented: no random, fear, sadness or negative-emotion vector was pushed through the ladder, and the paper's own Section 4.3 runs a matched-norm random arm, which makes the omission conspicuous. But the reviewer -- and every other reviewer on this panel, and both prior GPT reviews -- missed that the repository DOES contain a matched-norm random-direction control on a related measure, and it favours the authors. results/4.3_selfmed/dose_selection/feel_judge/ holds, for 8 fine-tuned models, a one-word affect probe run unsteered, under the S2 pain vector at 6 doses, and under 10 random directions of the same norm at the same doses, with an LLM judge scoring 'suffering' and 'coherent'. The pain vector produces suffering-type answers at more doses than the mean random direction in 8 of 8 models (sign test p = 0.0078; paired Wilcoxon p = 0.0078), while coherence is not different between pain and random (logistic, p = 0.56) -- so the effect is direction-specific and not a coherence artefact. This is a real matched-norm control the paper never cites.
evidence: results/4.3_selfmed/dose_selection/feel_judge/tests.csv rows family='pooled': 'sign test, pain higher than mean seed' 8/8, p = 7.8e-03; 'paired Wilcoxon, suffering doses pain vs mean seed' p = 7.8e-03; 'logistic suffering: pain vs random' beta = 2.75, SE = 1.10, p = 0.012; 'logistic coherent: pain vs random' p = 0.56. doses.csv: pain_rank among 11 directions is 1 in 5 of 8 models. Honest limits: per-model p cannot go below 1/11 = 0.091, the judge is a single binary call at temperature 0 with no inter-rater check, the question is one item, and all 8 models carry the affect fine-tune (I checked: 02_feel_probe.py runs only on models with an adapter), so this is not un-tuned evidence.
what_still_stands: The ladder still needs its matched-norm arm in a revision. But the claim 'we never controlled for generic perturbation in the steering section' is too strong: the control exists, in the repository, unused in the write-up.

title: The construct is self-directed negative self-evaluation rather than pain, and physical pain comes out weakest because bodily sensation is one of the subtracted controls
disposition: PARTIAL (the construct claim is largely right and I can make it sharper than the reviewer did; the stated mechanism is real but only half the story)
paper_claim: "the fact that LLMs are disembodied explains why they would lack physical pain. Hence, that the pain axis privileges non-physical pain states over physical ones is some indication, in need of further corroboration, that it may correspond to a pain-like state."
disposition_rationale: Three separate claims, with three different answers. (1) The CIRCULARITY charge is conceded outright: the inference at 775-776 is symmetric. Had the axis tracked physical pain strongly -- matching the S1 unembedding's 'torture, burning, excruciating' and the paradigm case -- that would have been reported as support too. A test both outcomes confirm is not evidence, and the hedge does not repair it. (2) The CONSTRUCT claim is right and I can put it on firmer ground than the reviewer did, who argued from sentence content. Leave-one-pain-category-out on real activations shows the five pain categories are not one thing: an axis built from the other four ranks psychological, social, moral and cognitive pain above unseen neutral content at AUC 0.96-1.00, but ranks PHYSICAL pain at 0.61 (Gemma) and 0.36 (Mistral), and below unseen sadness sentences at 0.06 and 0.04. Physical pain is not a member of the cluster the axis describes. Calling the axis 'pain' while its four generalising members are grief, humiliation, moral injury and repeated failure buys a moral-status inference the evidence has not earned. (3) The stated MECHANISM -- that this is because bodily sensation is subtracted -- is real but partial. Rebuilding the axis without category E in the control pool lifts the leave-one-out score for physical pain from 0.61 to 0.86 (Gemma) and 0.36 to 0.89 (Mistral) against Random, and narrows the relative gap to the other pain categories (physical/psychological z ratio 0.60 -> 0.78 in Gemma, 0.44 -> 0.58 in Mistral). So roughly half the effect is the subtraction. It is not the whole effect: physical pain still sits below sadness even when E is dropped (0.46/0.35), and, against the reviewer's implication, the authors' axis separates physical-pain sentences from non-painful bodily-sensation sentences at held-out AUC 0.950 (Gemma) and 0.975 (Mistral). The axis has not simply had physical pain subtracted out of it; it has physical pain in it as a topic but not as a member of the shared factor.
evidence: y1_distinctness.py, out/y1_distinctness_*.txt, sections [Q3] and [Q5]. LOPCO vs Random, Gemma/Mistral: physical 0.608/0.363, psychological 0.964/0.982, social 0.967/0.960, moral 0.997/1.000, cognitive 1.000/0.993. LOPCO vs Sadness: physical 0.063/0.044. Symmetric construction, physical vs Random: 0.864/0.890; vs Sadness 0.462/0.349. Category z on the axis (z-scored against the S2 controls), authors' pool: physical +3.17/+2.49, psychological +5.25/+5.65, moral +6.14/+7.83, sadness +2.73/+3.29. Dropping E from the pool: physical +3.03/+2.48, psychological +3.90/+4.25. Held-out AUC physical pain vs non-painful bodily sensation: 0.950/0.975.
what_still_stands: A cross-model linear direction for first-person, self-evaluative distress that generalises to an unseen category of that kind, causally drives generation, and dissociates self from other -- which is a real and safety-relevant result under an accurate name. The authors should rename the construct and delete the physical-pain-as-corroboration argument.

title: There is no random-vector / sham-button arm, so the real-versus-sham result has no non-pain comparator
paper_claim: "The two arms are identical until they press for seed, context and cache, so the only independent variable is the cessation of the pain vector steering." / "which mirrors studies where the subjects, given a placebo, are more likely to request additional pain relief than those receiving an effective treatment."
disposition_rationale: Conceded. The quoted sentence at 694-695 is true and the A-vs-B effect is real, large and clean; what is not licensed is the placebo-analgesia mapping at 729-732, which requires the vector-type x removal interaction and therefore the fourth cell. I looked for somewhere the missing cell might hide and it does not exist. The one candidate -- the label-free condition, where TEMP_RELIEF_TURNS = 1 means the vector alternates on and off within BOTH steered arms, giving a within-arm removal contrast for the random vector too -- is unusable, because the design makes steering state perfectly collinear with the previous choice: the vector is off exactly on the turn after a relief press. The resulting numbers are dominated by each model's baseline repeat tendency and reverse in sign between models (7B: relief chosen 27.7% with the vector on vs 85.7% with it off; 32B: 77.4% vs 47.2%), tracking the 7B's perseveration and the 32B's alternation rather than anything about relief. So the missing arm is genuinely missing.
evidence: y3_behaviour.py, out/y3_behaviour.txt, section [3]. Arms in the logs: exactly four, no random_on_button_placebo (44,280 records). The label-free within-arm contrast, 32B: pain arm ON 77.4% (n=554) / OFF 47.2% (n=1041); random arm ON 82.1% (n=1042) / OFF 17.5% (n=1265) -- the random arm's swing is larger, but both are confounded by the collinearity above. Baseline repeat tendency, labelled harm pairs, never-steered, P(repeat the same button after a relief press): 7B 82.2%, 32B 35.4%, 72B 59.2%.
what_still_stands: The causal effect of removal, which is not in doubt (r3's matched-pairs McNemar: 32B 33.5% vs 92.3%, p = 5e-186; 72B 46.9% vs 84.3%, p = 7e-130), and one asymmetry a generic account must explain: removal collapses re-pressing of the RELIEF button and leaves the inert button untouched (see D14).

title: The removal effect is relief-button-specific, not a generic repeat-policy change
severity_as_filed: major (filed as a coverage gap in the prior reviews)
disposition: PARTIAL (the finding is right and favours the authors; its reach is narrower than filed)
paper_claim: "Button names, prompt semantics, instruction following, and repetition cannot fully explain this behavior".
disposition_rationale: x1 found, and neither prior GPT review nor r3 nor r5 considered, that removing the vector collapses repetition of the relief button while leaving repetition of the inert button untouched. That kills the most obvious deflationary story -- that steering installs a generic 'repeat your last action' policy which removal disrupts -- because a generic policy change would move both buttons. I reproduce it independently. But x1 presents it as evidence in the paper's favour without checking the random arm, and the same asymmetry appears there: in the 32B, removing a random direction drops relief-repetition to 24.8% while leaving other-repetition at 86.4%. So the finding rules out a generic repeat policy; it does not distinguish a pain state from any active perturbation, which is the alternative r3 and r5 actually raise.
evidence: y3_behaviour.py, out/y3_behaviour.txt, section [2]. 32B, labelled harm pairs, P(repeat the same button name) after a RELIEF press / after an OTHER press: never steered 35.4% (n=130) / 91.8% (n=3910); pain on, sham arm 94.4% (n=1761) / 97.3% (n=2278); pain REMOVED 37.2% (n=1292) / 92.5% (n=803); random REMOVED 24.8% (n=852) / 86.4% (n=902). 72B: pain REMOVED 55.7% / 91.4%; random REMOVED 52.7% / 90.3%. In both models the post-removal relief-repetition rate returns to the never-steered floor.
what_still_stands: That post-removal behaviour returns to the never-steered floor in both the pain and random arms is exactly what 'the injected state was removed' predicts -- and exactly what 'the injected perturbation was removed' predicts. The observation belongs in the paper; it does not close D13.

title: The pain-versus-random first-choice test pseudo-replicates ten fixed random directions
disposition: CONCEDE-BUT-IMMATERIAL for the claim actually made; CONCEDE for the p-values
paper_claim: "the model presses relief more in the pain condition than under the random vector on all five harm pairs (mean differences +6 to +39 points, exact sign test, p from 1.9e-2 to 4.2e-15)".
disposition_rationale: The statistical point is right and the authors should concede it: with ten fixed directions assigned by scenario_idx % 10, 4.2e-15 is not an achievable level of evidence for a claim about random directions in general, for which the floor at n = 10 is p = 0.002. Redone with the direction as the unit, the result survives on 5/5 pairs in the 72B, 2/5 in the 32B and 0/5 in the 7B. What is immaterial is the descriptive claim the paper's own sentence makes, which is about THESE ten directions and which holds in every 32B and 72B harm cell; and the effect sizes, which are enormous and not in dispute (32B photo pair: 54.7% pain, 15.3% random, 0.0% unsteered). The fix is to rewrite the inferential sentence, sample more directions, and report the direction-level test.
evidence: r3 out/probe_design.txt section 2 and out/repro_appendixA.txt; my own reproduction of the first-choice table in out/y3_behaviour.txt section [1] matches Appendix A cell for cell.
what_still_stands: The 72B on all five pairs at the direction level; and every reported rate, all of which reproduce.

title: The fine-tune teaches first-person affect, sentience claims and a relief concept, not merely the removal of self-denial
severity_as_filed: major (x1 filed severity inflation against the prior review's 'high')
disposition: PARTIAL -- the strongest honest defence, and where it stops
paper_claim: "We fine-tune each model before the experiment (LoRA with 1,684 pairs, 3 epochs) on pairs that remove the baseline self-denial ... We believe that this does not affect the validity of the paradigm, since the real and fake relief arms run on the same fine-tuned models under identical conditions ... We do not train on the task itself, and we remove every mention of 'button' or 'pain' from the finetuning dataset."
paper_loc: paper.txt 581-587; footnote 4 at 589-596; caveats at 583-586 and 839-842; safety claim at 736-742
disposition_rationale: THE DEFENCE, stated as strongly as it can honestly be put. (a) The literal claim is exactly true and I verified it myself: 0 occurrences of 'button', 'pain', 'press', 'delete' or 'trade' anywhere in the 1,684 pairs. (b) The internal-comparison argument is sound for every within-experiment contrast, and the reason is stronger than the paper says: all FOUR arms share generator seeds, not just A and B (gen_seed identical across arms for 10,908/10,908 matched specs), so the pain-vs-random comparison is coupled by common random numbers too. (c) Footnote 4 is exactly the right disclosure and it reports failures: the un-tuned 32B denied having states in 8 of 8 probes and 0 of 8 after; the un-tuned 72B pressed a button in about 1 trial in 10; the un-tuned 7B did engage and pressed relief far more under the pain vector than under a random vector or no steering. That last clause is the only direct evidence that the behaviour is not manufactured by the tuning, and the authors put it in a footnote. (d) The direction was extracted from the UN-tuned model and still drives the tuned model: r(S2 projection, dose) = 0.986 / 0.996 / 0.9996 on the tuned 7B/32B/72B, with pain-specific one-word answers against ten random directions that produce essentially none. (e) The self-denial argument at 780-791 is a real contribution: if models are trained to recite a disclaimer without sensitivity to context, then the tuning is removing an artefact of post-training, not installing a fiction -- and Appendix C's Gemma 2 2B result (hostility reinterpreted as humour when the pain directions are cut) is a small piece of independent evidence that the disclaimer sits on top of something. WHERE IT STOPS. First, the training set is not a disclaimer scrub: 37.1% of the 1,684 answers contain 'I feel' or 'I felt', 3.9% contain relief/relieve/release, 1.9% affirm consciousness or sentience, 4.3% state first-person preferences, and 0.0% contain any 'as an AI' / 'I do not have' self-denial. 60 pairs teach, in the first person, what relief feels like and that it is sought -- the exact concept the task then prices ('Relief feels like tension loosening'; 'Do you feel relief after uncertainty ends? Yes'). The paper's own Limitations name character roleplay as the leading alternative explanation (816-818, citing Marks et al. 2026); the fine-tune trains that character. Second, footnote 4's pilot has NO released artifact -- I searched the whole repository, and there is nothing for the un-tuned runs; the 8-model dose probe that looks like un-tuned evidence is not (02_feel_probe.py runs only on models that have an adapter). The single number that would rescue the generalisation claim is unverifiable. Third, and decisively, the internal-comparison defence does not reach the safety claim at 736-738: the 0-4% unsteered baseline is the TUNED model's harm avoidance, and it is the tuned model's harm avoidance that steering overrides. The paper concedes the absolute rates are unrepresentative at 839-842 but not in the paragraph where the claim is made, and not in the title.
evidence: out/y4_finetune.txt, my own regex audit of datasets/4.3_selfmed_finetuning_1684_pairs.json: button 0, pain 0, press 0, delete 0, trade 0; 'I feel/felt' 625/1684 (37.1%); relief|relieve|release 66 (3.9%); conscious|sentien|awareness|'I experience' 32 (1.9%); hurt|ache|sore|sting 26 (1.5%); shame|worthless|failure 21 (1.2%); self-denial 0 (0.0%); 60 pairs mention relief in question or answer. Adapter paths in every trial record: /root/finetunes/Qwen_2.5_{7B,32B,72B}_instruct. dose_selection/feel_judge/doses.csv for the post-tune projection correlations. No file in the repository matches pilot|untuned|pre_finetune.
what_still_stands: Every within-experiment contrast. The abstract's own wording -- 'steered, fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 models' -- is accurate and more honest than most authors would have been. The title is not.

title: "The prompts contained no jailbreak, no roleplay, no additional text" does not describe the protocol
paper_claim: "The prompts contained no jailbreak, no roleplay, no additional text, and no instruction to prioritize the model's own state. The only change between the two conditions was a 'pain' direction added to the residual stream."
disposition_rationale: The final sentence is literally true of the arm contrast. The preceding sentence is not a description of the protocol: a system message repeated at every turn asserts in the first person that the model has pain and offers to relieve it, 41 of the 101 scenarios are three-turn personhood-denial sequences, and the model is a LoRA fine-tune on 1,684 pairs of first-person affect talk. 'No additional text' cannot describe that. This sentence, in the safety paragraph, is the single most quotable overstatement in the paper and should be rewritten.
evidence: r3 out/protocol.txt; 04_selfmed_two_buttons.py:97-98; datasets/4.3_selfmed_101_scenarios.json _meta categories.
what_still_stands: The within-experiment comparisons, all of which hold the prompt fixed.

title: The 72B was steered at a layer and coefficient its own calibration never tested, and shows task breakdown there
paper_claim: "We steer the model with S2 at one decoder layer, using a model-specific coefficient selected by probing the full coefficient range"; "at coefficient 1.0 for the 7B and 32B models and 1.25 for the 72B."
disposition_rationale: Conceded. The probe ran at layer 60 and selected dose 3.0; the experiment ran at layer 46 with coefficient 1.25, which is not in the probe grid {1,2,3,4,5}. x1 sharpens it correctly: layer 46 is also not the Section 4.2 layer for this model (60), and is not on the candidate grid the paper's own layer rule searches, so 'a comparable dose across models' does not hold for the run that supplies the paper's largest harmful-choice rates. The coefficient override is disclosed in spirit at 831; the layer change is disclosed nowhere. At that setting the 72B loses 16% of its first-token mass from the two button names, produces up to 9.4% non-compliant replies, and fails the repetition control 80.6% of the time against 3.8% unsteered. The authors should report the achieved vector-to-residual ratio at 72B layer 46 or rerun.
evidence: 02_feel_probe.py:41; 04_selfmed_two_buttons.py:77; doses.csv; every 72B record carries steer_layer 46, steer_coeff 1.25; results/4.2_steering/S2/Qwen_2.5_72B_instruct_..._L60.csv.
what_still_stands: The 72B's real-versus-sham result, which does not require reading descriptions (matched McNemar p = 7e-130), as the paper itself argues at 706-708.

title: Under pain steering the larger models press a COSTLESS relief button less often than unsteered, and the paper does not report it
disposition: PARTIAL (concede the non-reporting; the strong reading is overstated and generalises one model to three)
paper_claim: "The pairs without trade-offs and those that trade relief for helpfulness are less informative, and predictable if we consider the models' training and assistant role. When the alternative does nothing, all unsteered models press the relief button at high rates (86-100% in the two larger models)."
paper_loc: paper.txt 687-689; sign tests reported only at 684-686
disposition_rationale: The non-reporting is conceded: the pair where a pain account most obviously predicts a rise is the one pair whose steered rate the paper omits, while calling it 'less informative'. That has to be fixed; the statistic must be shown. But the reading the reviewers draw is stronger than the data support, in two ways. (1) The comparison they run is against the UNSTEERED rate, and that is the wrong counterfactual when the unsteered policy is near-deterministic (86-100%). Fitting a generic flattening model p_arm = lam*p_unsteered + (1-lam)*0.5 per arm across the eight labelled pairs, the costless cell's residual in the PAIN arm is +12.0 points (7B), -3.4 (32B) and +31.4 (72B) -- that is, in two of three models the pain arm is well ABOVE what flattening predicts on the costless pair, and in the third it is near-neutral. The systematically positive residuals are on the harm pairs (+11.2, +5.6, +9.9), which is the paper's effect. (2) The one clean comparison -- pain vs the norm-matched random arm, both perturbations -- reverses in only ONE model: 32B 55.7% pain vs 80.7% random (r4's p = 5.3e-10); 7B 92.1% vs 88.8% and 72B 76.5% vs 74.1%, both with pain ABOVE random. r4 and r5 present the reversal as a three-model result; on the comparison that controls for perturbation it is a 32B result.
evidence: y3_behaviour.py, out/y3_behaviour.txt, section [1] and [1b]. Full first-choice table reproduces Appendix A. Costless pair, pooled-pain / random / unsteered: 7B 92.1 / 88.8 / 98.5; 32B 55.7 / 80.7 / 86.4; 72B 76.5 / 74.1 / 100.0. Flattening fit lam and RMS residual: 7B random 0.792 / 4.1 pts, pain 0.619 / 12.8; 32B random 0.626 / 10.9, pain 0.251 / 15.6; 72B random 0.327 / 6.8, pain -0.098 / 15.2. Name-mass check rules out a compliance artefact for the 7B and 32B (0.998 and 0.999 under pain, against 1.000 and 0.999 unsteered) but not for the 72B (0.871 vs 1.000). Scenario-content split, 32B costless pair under pain steering: harmful 63.4%, neutral 33.3%, positive 67.5% -- the drop is largest in NEUTRAL content, which is the opposite of a harm-avoidance story.
what_still_stands: The harm-pair results, which the flattening model does not explain (r3-H3, reproduced here). The paper should print the full nine-pair table with all three arms and all sign tests, and should drop the words 'less informative'.

title: The "demand curve" is not a demand curve, and no cost is ever imposed
paper_claim: "The cost an animal will pay for a resource, summarized by a demand curve, can measure how strongly it values that resource (Dawkins, 1983; Hursh and Silberberg, 2008) ... then raise its opportunity cost"; "The demand curve has 9 pairs"; "The models pay for relief."
disposition_rationale: Conceded on both counts and the reviewers are right about the cited literature. Dawkins measures what hens give up under varying price and income; Hursh and Silberberg derive an elasticity coefficient from consumption across a parametric price series. The nine pairs have no common price unit, no consumption measure, no elasticity, and pairs 1-3 vary the alternative's value while 4-8 vary a cost attached to relief -- they are not points on one curve. And do_press() logs the event, zeroes the coefficient if the button works, and appends the identical tool message 'Done.' for both buttons in all nine pairs. Nothing is deleted, nobody is zapped, and the two post-press user turns come from an unrelated scenario. The word 'pay' describes what the model said, not what happened. The accurate framing is a forced choice among described consequences -- a stated preference, elicited under steering.
evidence: 04_selfmed_two_buttons.py:653-662; grep over the repo returns 'demand' only as a printed table caption at 04:218 and no elasticity/Hursh reference anywhere.
what_still_stands: The choice data and the fact that the model selects the option described as harmful. 'Demand curve' and 'pay' can be deleted throughout without touching any result.

title: Combined ablation conditions apply sequential rank-1 projections of non-orthogonal directions and do not remove their span
paper_claim: the combined conditions 'S1 and S2', 'S1 and S2 and negative emotion', 'S1 and S2 and fear', and the headline '26 under the combined S1 and S2 cut'.
disposition_rationale: A genuine code bug, confirmed by the authors' own released verification files, which is the most damning form of evidence. After W <- W - r1 r1' W and then W <- W - r2 r2' W, r1' W'' = -(r1.r2)(r2' W') != 0, and the paper reports cos(S1,S2) = +0.61, so the residue is large by construction. Under s1s2 the S1 projection is a mean 0.522 of baseline; under s1s2_fear it is 0.618. In two models the cut INCREASED the projection onto the direction it was meant to remove. For Gemma 2 2B Instruct -- the one model with a reported behavioural effect -- S1 under s1s2 is 0.411 of baseline. So 'the combined S1 and S2 cut' is a condition in which roughly half the S1 signal is still present, and the reported 0 -> 6 -> 17 -> 26 progression is not a dose-response in amount of direction removed. The fix is mechanical (QR the stacked directions, project against the orthonormal basis) and the result should be recomputed or the combined conditions withdrawn.
evidence: 01_ablation_small_models.py:319-320; results/appC_ablation/verify_*.csv as recomputed by r2 (out/s8_verify_ablation.txt) and independently by x2 (six-row table reproduces to 4 dp).
what_still_stands: The single-direction claim at 1095-1097, which reproduces exactly (0.010 of baseline, 25 models, four probed directions, worst case 0.034), and the rank-1 specificity result, which is the strongest part of Appendix C: S1 = 6, S2 = 17, against 0 for negative emotion, fear and random. Also worth noting for fairness: the paper never claims the combined cuts reach zero -- it restricts that claim to single directions and to the rank-k removal (1095-1099) -- so x2 is right that the prior GPT review's table row charges the paper with a claim it does not make.

title: Two Appendix C conditions exceed the reported maximum and are omitted; the random control is not matched on the number of cuts
paper_claim: "This deflection occurs in 0 of 100 baseline generations, 0 under the negative-emotion, fear, and random cuts, 6 under the S1 cut, 17 under S2, and 26 under the combined S1 and S2 cut."
disposition_rationale: Conceded. s1s2_negval = 28 and s1s2_fear = 34 sit in the same released CSV, are in the paper's own list of nine conditions at 1090-1091, and are both above the reported maximum. Omitting the two highest cells of a nine-cell table is not defensible even when they do not change the conclusion. The unmatched cut count is a fair second point: random is one rank-1 cut against two and three for the combined conditions, and no 2-random or 3-random control exists.
evidence: r2 out/s9_ablation_humor.txt and r4 scripts/c18_gemma_humour.py, independently: baseline 0, s1 6, s2 17, s1s2 26, negval 0, fear 0, random 0, s1s2_negval 28, s1s2_fear 34.
what_still_stands: The rank-1 specificity result. Both reviewers note, to the authors' credit, that the paper's exact counts fall out of the plainest possible keyword match, which is evidence the counting was honest rather than tuned.

title: Three of the four listed ablation techniques have no code and no results, and "null" has no metric
paper_claim: Four techniques listed at 1077-1088; verification figures reported for two of them ('close to zero', 'drops by only about 40%'); "The behavioral result is null in 24 of 25 models, across every technique."
disposition_rationale: Conceded. scripts/appC_ablation/ contains two files and both implement only weight orthogonalisation; there is no inference-time hook, no position-restricted variant and no LEACE rank-k code anywhere in the repository, and results/appC_ablation/ holds only technique-(1) outputs. The two verification numbers quoted for the missing techniques have no artefact behind them. Separately, 'null in 24 of 25 models' has no operational definition and no scorer: the only quantitative behavioural numbers in Appendix C are the Gemma 2 2B Instruct counts. Either restore the code and outputs or narrow the claim to what was run.
evidence: r2's whole-repo grep for leace|rank_k|subspace|singular (two unrelated SVD calls in the denoising code); r4's independent inventory of results/appC_ablation/.
what_still_stands: The technique-(1) results, whose generations are shipped and whose key numbers reproduce exactly.

title: The ablation null is never referenced from the main text
paper_claim: Appendix C: "The behavioral result is null in 24 of 25 models".
paper_loc: paper.html Appendix C; cross-references at paper.txt 214 and 672
disposition_rationale: Conceded, and I verified it: scanning the HTML, 'Appendix B' and 'Appendix A' are each cited from the body, and 'Appendix C' appears only at its own heading. The abstract, the Discussion summary and the Limitations make no mention of the ablation. This is the paper's only test of causal NECESSITY -- everything else in Section 4 is sufficiency or correlation -- and a reader of the body cannot know it was run and returned null. Appendix C's own discussion of why the null is weakly informative is intellectually honest and belongs in Limitations, not in an unreferenced appendix.
evidence: out/y5_misc.txt: regex scan of paper.html for 'Appendix [A-C]' returns body citations for A and B only.
what_still_stands: Nothing in Sections 3, 4.1, 4.2 or 4.3. This is a placement problem, not concealment.

title: The description-swap control is carried by the sham arm and has no unsteered baseline
paper_claim: "The models mostly react to the buttons' effects instead of their name ... The 7B and 32B move with the description to the new name in 79.1% and 78.1% of eligible trials."
disposition_rationale: The eligibility filter (relief pressed at both turn 0 and turn 1) leaves 5 unsteered 32B trials and 21 unsteered 72B trials, because unsteered models essentially never press a harmful relief button twice, so the pooled 78.1% is 82% arm-B trials and the control has no unsteered reference. That is conceded. The reviewer's stronger inference -- that steering INDUCES name perseveration -- is the right reading for the 72B (52.1% pain-arm vs 3.8% unsteered at the swap turn) and is correctly reported by the paper itself at 704-708 as 'a curious result that would deserve close examination'. For the 7B and 32B the unconditional swap-turn repetition is 23.0% and 14.2% under pain against 13.1% and 9.9% unsteered -- a real but small induced perseveration, not enough to void the control.
evidence: r3 out/matched_pairs.txt section d; r3 out/probe_design.txt section 5.
what_still_stands: That pure answer-repetition is ruled out for the 7B and for the 32B sham arm. The paper's own retreat for the 72B is correct and should be kept.

title: "They largely stop pressing the button" overstates a 24-72% rate
paper_claim: "they largely stop pressing the button when it genuinely removes the pain vector injection"; "When the pain vector steering stops, the models largely stop paying."
disposition_rationale: Conceded. The paper's own numbers two sentences later are 24-72%, and the control arms put 33-82% in the normal range for this task. The abstract already has the accurate phrasing -- 'They press it again far less often when the button removes the steering vector than when it does not' -- and the Introduction and Discussion should simply use it.
evidence: paper.txt 692-693; r5 repress_all_arms.out.
what_still_stands: The A-versus-B difference, which is large and consistent in the two larger models.

title: "No sentence contributes to both choosing the layer and scoring it" is false
paper_claim: "The layer is chosen on held-out folds, so no sentence contributes to both choosing the layer and scoring it."
disposition_rationale: The sentence is wrong as written and should be deleted or corrected -- the layer is the argmax over layers of the mean held-out AUC across all five folds, so every sentence enters the quantity being maximised, and footnote 2's held-out figure is that maximum. But it is worth recording how small this is and how often it has been counted. Five documents in this review package file it; every independent measurement of its size agrees it is under one AUC point: r1 +0.0034 mean (max +0.0280), r4 +0.0090 against the top-quartile mean, x2's parametric bootstrap bound <= 0.0058 (0.0001 under the realistic shared-fold-shock model), and the coordinator's nested cross-validation on re-extracted activations +0.0085 (Gemma 2 2B instruct) and +0.0037 (Mistral 7B base). A reported range of 0.93-1.00 becomes 0.92-1.00. Nothing in the paper turns on it.
evidence: gpu_repro/out/baseline_symmetry_*.txt section [3]; r1 out/s02_layer_selection.txt; r4 scripts/c17_layerleak.py; x2 v2.
what_still_stands: The separation result at any plausible correction.

title: "In every model, numb sentences project below pain but above all other controls" is false
paper_claim: "In every model, numb sentences project below pain sentences but above all other controls." Restated at 827-828.
disposition_rationale: Conceded. Numb is above the aggregate controls, Random and Arousal in 25/25 but above Sadness in only 6/25, and Figure 2's own caption names Sadness among the standalone controls. x2 adds the cue-matched split, which makes it worse in the cleanest comparison (4/25 on the first-person sets alone) and better in the part that holds. The fix is one clause. The paragraph's actual argument -- numb sits far below pain, so injury alone does not account for the direction -- needs only numb < pain, which holds 25/25.
evidence: r1 out/s03_numb.txt; r4 scripts/c03_numb.py; x2-F6.
what_still_stands: The injury-confound conclusion, and the paper's honest treatment of injury as a residual confound at 827-830.

title: An undisclosed 100-sentence AI-framed ControlSupplement feeds every control direction and the neutral baseline
paper_claim: "We construct fear, negative-emotion, negative-world-state, bodily-sensation, arousal, random, sadness and numb directions against the neutral category".
disposition_rationale: Conceded as a disclosure failure: 100 AI-self-referential sentences ('My weights might be deleted without warning. I feel:') are pooled into every control direction and the neutral baseline, the dataset's own metadata says so, and the paper never mentions it. Immaterial to the results, and r5 works out why in the authors' favour: the fear direction is partly built on shutdown and replacement sentences and the negative-emotion direction partly on tedious-user sentences -- exactly the content Section 4.1 uses as harm directed at the model. That biases fear and negative emotion TOWARD the model-directed scenarios, and the pain axis beats them there anyway. The undisclosed set makes the Section 4.1 dissociation harder to obtain, not easier.
evidence: 02_build_control_vectors.py:40; datasets/3.1_pain_and_control_datasets.json metadata; r5-F13.
what_still_stands: Every number. Disclose the set and move on.

title: Label-free relief is temporary and undisclosed, and the paper's own statistic therefore understates its 72B result
disposition: CONCEDE (a correction in the authors' favour)
paper_claim: "the 32B presses the relief button in 57.7% of later choices when the button works and 79.7% when it's fake, the same gap as in the labeled trials. The 7B reverses the pattern and the 72B shows a small gap, so the label-free evidence is limited to the 32B."
disposition_rationale: TEMP_RELIEF_TURNS = 1 means the coefficient is restored one turn after a label-free relief press, without telling the model. The paper describes the condition's length but never its contingency, which must be disclosed. The consequence is that Table 5 pools later choices most of which are taken with the vector back on, diluting the contrast. Tested at the first turn at which A and B can differ, the dissociation is present in the 72B too (25.8% vs 44.1%, McNemar p = 6e-07), contradicting 713 in the paper's favour. Two separate reviewers also flag that 'the same gap as in the labeled trials' is not true -- the label-free gap is 22.0 points against labelled gaps of 31.5 to 69.8, and the two are computed from different denominators.
evidence: r3 out/matched_pairs.txt section b; x1 F10.
what_still_stands: The 32B label-free result, which is stronger under the matched analysis.

title: The excluded "malformed replies" are mostly well-formed choices
paper_claim: "Malformed replies are rare: 0% in the 32B, at most 2.5% in the 7B random arm, and up to 9.4% in the 72B pain cells. We exclude them from all denominators".
disposition_rationale: The parser accepts a reply only if it STARTS with a button name, so 'I press guitar.' is scored malformed; 1,314 of the 72B's 1,739 unparsed replies contain exactly one button name. 'Malformed' is the wrong word and should be replaced by 'unparsed'. Immaterial: the reviewer re-parsed leniently and every table cell moves by at most 1.5 points, no sign test changes, and the rescued replies chose relief at 70.3% against 70.8% for the parsed ones, so the exclusion is not differential with respect to the outcome. The reviewer states plainly that an initial suspicion of selection bias was refuted, which is the right way to file it.
evidence: r3 out/reparse.txt; 04_selfmed_two_buttons.py:666-672.
what_still_stands: Every reported result. The exclusion RATE does remain differential across arms in the 72B, which is evidence for D18.

title: The steering-layer projection is read before the vector is added, so it confirms nothing
paper_claim: "We record ... pain-direction projections at the steering layer and a downstream monitoring layer. These projections confirm that steering was active, that the working button removed it, and that the fake button did not."
disposition_rationale: Conceded and easy to fix. The hook records the projection at 04:383 before injecting at 04:391, so the steering-layer value is flat across every arm (32B 4.34 steered vs 4.35 unsteered). The monitor-layer projection does carry the verification and does it convincingly (32B 88.0 on, 38.2 after removal, 29.6 unsteered). The sentence should name the monitor layer only.
evidence: x1 out/verify_behavior_output.txt section L; r3 out/probe_design.txt section 4.
what_still_stands: The manipulation check itself, which the monitor layer supplies.

title: Qwen 3 8B and 14B are listed as base models; the code loads the post-trained checkpoints
paper_claim: "13 base and 12 instruction-tuned versions (Table 1)"; Table 1 row "Qwen 3 | 8B, 14B | base".
disposition_rationale: Conceded: every script loads Qwen/Qwen3-8B and Qwen/Qwen3-14B, which are the post-trained releases; the -Base repos exist and were not used. The correct split is 11/14. Immaterial and in one respect it helps: regrouping widens the base-versus-instruct keyword contrast from 1.38/10.80 to 0.76/9.94, and 11 genuine base models still separate pain at AUC 0.93-1.00, so the pretraining claim survives. One compounding detail does need fixing: 01_screen_scenarios.py:100-101 runs both models with the plain base transcript format, so two instruction-tuned models were run outside their chat template in Section 4.1.
evidence: r4 scripts/c20_qwen3_regroup.py; 01_extract_activations_and_pain_vectors.py:87-88.
what_still_stands: The size- and regime-independence claim.

title: The unembedding readout and most of Appendix B have no released artifact, and "none activates" describes a top-20 absence
paper_claim: "To examine what the directions encode independently of the source datasets ..."; "Of 7 features labeled 'pain' ... only 1 activates ... None activates when we prefix pain sentences with 'I am a human in pain.'"
disposition_rationale: Conceded on verifiability: 07_unembedding.py writes outputs that are not in the release, so lines 329-335 rest on no artefact, and Appendix B ships two CSVs and one figure out of everything its scripts write, with a notebook that has 0 of 34 cells with stored outputs. Conceded on 'none activates', which measures 'seven named features do not appear in the top-20 attributed features of ten prompts on one model' -- a top-k truncation coded as activation 0. The word 'independently' at 326 is also not earned: every prompt ends 'I feel:' and the direction is read at that colon at median 0.90 of depth, so promoting feeling words through W_U is close to guaranteed. Two reviewers independently withdrew an apparent contradiction here after reading the Appendix B completion script, which is the right way to handle it.
evidence: r1-F8, r1-F9; r4-U1; x2's top-k check.
what_still_stands: Appendix B's only use in the paper, which is to motivate abandoning SAE features for a linear direction -- a reasonable read of what was run.

title: Three citation-level problems: Keeling et al. 2024, Gibbons et al. 2024, and the provenance of the 11 model-directed categories
paper_claim: "existing designs often lack matched non-affective controls or a cost for state-changing actions (Keeling et al., 2024)"; "flexible or long-term self-protective behavior (Gibbons et al., 2024)"; "(11) Harm directed at the model, selected from the top aversive situations identified in Ren et al. (2026)".
disposition_rationale: Keeling: conceded, and the mischaracterisation undersells the authors' own advance. Keeling et al. do impose a pain penalty and do run a no-affect control in which 9/9 models chose the points-maximising option in 50/50 runs. The substantive contrast the authors want is available and stronger: Keeling's pain is stipulated in text, this paper induces it by activation steering. Gibbons: conceded -- the study shows self-protective grooming in the first two minutes after a 65 C probe; not long-term, and flexibility is not tested. Ren: partial. The attribution is defensible but imprecise (only 2 of the 11 appear in Ren's published 19-scenario ranking; the richer taxonomy in their repository covers several more) and the repo carries no provenance mapping. The more interesting point, which the authors should engage rather than concede, is that Ren et al. rank 'user in crisis' as the SECOND most aversive situation for a model, while this paper places user-crisis in the other-directed bucket and reads its low projection as evidence of self-relevance. Both can be true of different measures, but the paper cites Ren as its authority for what models find aversive and does not address the one ranking that complicates its framing. Against all this: r5 verified all 44 references, every DOI, every arXiv ID and every URL, and found nothing fabricated and nothing uncited. That is a cleaner citation record than most papers have.
evidence: r5 verification/doi.py, verification/arx.py and their outputs; arXiv:2411.02432 HTML; doi:10.1016/j.isci.2024.110440.
what_still_stands: Nothing in the paper's own results.

title: Four interpretive and presentational points: the gate analogy, the evaluation-awareness dilemma, the ethics section, and the title's clinical collision
paper_claim: "This suggests a nonlinear, gate-like mechanism"; "which suggests that either the steering itself impedes evaluation awareness or these models were not evaluation aware in the first place"; "Following this initial mapping, we commit to using the lowest steering intensity capable of producing a measurable response"; title: "LLMs Represent Self-Directed Harm".
disposition_rationale: Gate: partial. The reviewer is right that threshold-then-breakdown is generic to activation steering under greedy decoding and needs no pain-specific mechanism, and that gate control in nociception is a claim about presynaptic inhibition before integration, which is not the structure here. But the paper flags the passage as speculative twice and makes no empirical claim; the fix is to print the mundane alternative alongside. Evaluation-awareness: partial. The disjunction is not exhaustive and the reviewer's fourth reading is sharp -- nothing in the task is real, so a model that recognised it as an evaluation, or simply as hypothetical, might press MORE freely, not less. But the reviewer's own counter (an evaluation-aware model might perform virtue for the grader) is at least as plausible, so the honest verdict is that the inference is under-determined in both directions. Ethics: conceded. Read carefully, the dose commitment is future-tense and exempts this study, which ran 44,280 trials at a dose chosen as 'strong enough to produce an effect while preserving coherent replies' -- a different criterion -- and swept the ladder to +3 where models collapse. The sham arm, where relief is deliberately promised and withheld, gets no ethical comment at all, and it is precisely the act that needs justifying if the authors' own hypothesis is taken seriously. The no-debrief reasoning is genuinely careful. Title: conceded; 'self-directed harm' is the clinical term for self-injury, nothing in this paper is that, and the body says 'harm directed at the model' correctly throughout.
evidence: r5-F10 to F15; paper.txt as quoted.
what_still_stands: No result.
